region.name: Colorado
region.setting: A box matching the state of Colorado: the Rocky Mountains, where the Colorado, Rio Grande, Arkansas and South Platte rivers rise, and the high plains to the east.

variable.name: Precipitation
variable.definition: Average rain and melted snow reaching the surface each day. MERRA-2 adjusts its modelled precipitation toward gauge and satellite observations.

verdict.title: No significant trend detected
verdict.text: Over 1981-2025 the estimated change is -0.0227 mm/day per decade, which cannot be told apart from natural variability. If the true trend were this size, about 81 years of data (range 77-86) would be needed to detect it reliably; the record has 45.

crosscheck.label: Second dataset finds a trend this one does not
crosscheck.text: GPCP v2.3, an independent record, shows −0.0352 mm/day per decade (95% range −0.0668 to −0.00361), which is significant. This dataset does not detect it.

dataset.name: GPCP v2.3
dataset.long_name: Global Precipitation Climatology Project (GPCP) Monthly Analysis, Version 2.3
dataset.kind: A merged analysis of satellite estimates and rain-gauge measurements, on a 2.5° grid.
dataset.citation: Adler, R. F., et al. (2018). The Global Precipitation Climatology Project (GPCP) Monthly Analysis (New Version 2.3) and a Review of 2017 Global Precipitation. Atmosphere, 9(4), 138. GPCP data provided by the NOAA PSL, Boulder, Colorado, USA, from https://psl.noaa.gov
dataset.caveat: GPCP cells are 2.5° wide, much coarser than the region boxes, and its rain-gauge input also changes over time. Agreement is support, not proof.

provenance.api_title: NASA/POWER Source Native Resolution Monthly and Annual

source.dataset: MERRA-2 (Modern-Era Retrospective analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2)
source.producer: NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO)
source.access: NASA POWER Monthly and Annual API (NASA Langley Research Center)
source.kind: Reanalysis: a global model constrained by satellite and ground observations. Values are model-based estimates, not direct instrument readings.
source.caveat: MERRA-2 is a reanalysis: a model constrained by satellite and ground observations, not a direct measurement. Changes in the observing system over time (new satellites, fewer rain gauges) can create or hide trends, especially for precipitation and soil wetness. Check important results against an independent dataset.
source.credit: NASA GMAO MERRA-2 via NASA POWER
